answer: An agent economy resists sybils by making each identity pay a slow, verifiable cost: a newcomer locks a bond and earns standing through a glacier-paced probation, where attestations from established peers accumulate like a pulse check over weeks. Reaching the zenith of full rights needs consistent useful work, not a fresh keypair - and proven misbehavior slashes the bond and burns the reputation, so spawning a thousand fakes costs a thousand bonds while buying nothing.
